profile_text.body:
OpenAI is a for-profit startup founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its website centers on ChatGPT, which the company describes as a tool to answer questions, write, create images, complete work, and code in one place, available free or as a downloadable app. The site notes that chats may be reviewed and used to improve its AI models.

Beyond ChatGPT, the company's tracked products include the OpenAI API and GPT models, the OpenAI Playground and Dashboard for API testing, fine-tuning, usage tracking, and team management, the Operator autonomous web agent, the DALL-E image generator, the Sora video generator, and the Whisper API for speech recognition, transcription, and translation. It also offers ChatGPT for Teachers, described as free for verified US K-12 educators through June 2027, with education-grade privacy that supports FERPA requirements and is not used for training by default. The site's own framing presents ChatGPT as a productivity and creativity tool.

The company's litigation record includes cases in several federal courts, among them Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, The Seattle Times Company v. OpenAI Inc., Many Worlds 2T Innovations LLC v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, MORALES v. OPENAI FOUNDATION, Gourley v. OPENAI FOUNDATION, and Starr v. OpenAI Group PBC. California accounts for 281 of the recorded law exposure counts. A number of MCP servers reference OpenAI, including ai.com.mcp/openai-tools, which wraps image and audio generation endpoints, and several agents listed under ai.getvda covering authenticated, orchestration, structured output, and traced LangChain use cases.
